artworks.title: Roots of My Ancestors
artworks.medium: Oil paint, acrylic paint, canvas, perforated plastic non-slip mat painted with acrylics, needle and thread, yarn, metal mesh, wood panel, knitted garments, cyanotype prints, mirror
artworks.description: I created self-portraits on materials reminiscent of my childhood, juxtaposing these paintings against the backdrop of my mother’s garden, a slice of her life in her hometown. Including myself reflects how my family history lives through me. With this piece, I hope to depict the balance of life as an immigrant.

artworks.title: Fading in and Out
artworks.medium: Oil paint, acrylic paint, canvas, perforated plastic non-slip mat painted with acrylics, needle and thread, yarn
artworks.description: I used this variety of materials to create the effect that this piece is fragmented. As an Asian American, I often feel like certain parts of my identity fade in and out for the comfort of the people around me. Through this piece, I try to communicate this sense of adaptability to the viewer.

artworks.title: Rooted in Bamboo
artworks.medium: Colored pencil on Bristol paper, canvas, hot glue
artworks.description: My cat symbolizes a new chapter of my life since her adoption coincided with my move. Bamboo alludes to my Chinese heritage. I created this piece to encapsulate a feeling of warmth as a result of merging pieces of my identity together rather than viewing them as separate parts of a whole.
artworks.alt: Mixed media drawing titled Rooted in Bamboo with layered bamboo-like structures and green, cream, and dark forms.

artworks.title: Garden of Identity
artworks.medium: Oil paint, acrylic paint, handmade wood panel, bamboo strips, hand-grown flowers, mirror, watercolor paper, hot glue, hand saw
artworks.description: I painted candid self-portraits, incorporating mirror shards to symbolize my belief that my childhood self had to be shattered for me to grow. Mounted on bamboo and planted outdoors, these paintings represent my growing identity. I hoped to communicate the idea that identity is not a solid concept and is instead evolving.

artworks.title: Society's Box
artworks.medium: Acrylic paint, plaster casting, wooden box
artworks.description: The hands represent society's pressure on my evolving understanding of womanhood and how it differs from restrictive social expectations. Commercial red nail polish contrasts with my mother’s village recipe from China, revealing the hidden stories of womanhood. I made this piece to demonstrate how society does not leave enough space for women to thrive.

artworks.title: Is It All a Fabrication?
artworks.medium: Organza, lace, alcohol markers, water-based and oil-based face paint, nail polish, face mask, hand
artworks.description: In this piece, I explored how personal biases distort my perception of reality. Inspired by Ming pots, I painted my hand with face paint and used a face mask solution to mimic the shine of porcelain, a technique popularized by Pat McGrath. The composition suggests my own influence in making up fabrications about the world, represented by the fabric of the handkerchief I created. I hope to reveal my question about what reality truly is through this piece.
artworks.alt: Mixed material installation titled Is It All a Fabrication? using fabric, cosmetics, and hand-based forms.

artworks.title: Shining Through the Blue
artworks.medium: Yarn, crochet, cyanotype, golden GAC 400
artworks.description: I altered the stereotypically American T-shirt using crocheted strips and faint family photographs, bridging my two cultural identities. The second view features the Four Gentlemen, motifs my grandmother often depicted in her own art. Through this piece, I aim to reveal to the viewer how family continues shaping my identity despite geographical distance.

artworks.title: Lunch
artworks.medium: Terracotta, tin foil, newsprint, colored pencil, copper wire, yarn
artworks.description: This piece juxtaposes my lunch and my cousin’s lunch, emphasizing the difference between the two realities. Despite originally photographing these two lunches as separate, I chose to use yarn to suspend my lunch, erasing the lines between our realities. Through this piece, I hope to demonstrate how realities can coexist despite differences.

artworks.title: Versions of Me
artworks.medium: Wood panel, yarn, acrylic paint, colored pencil, drawing paper
artworks.description: In this piece, I chose to combine imagery of my two cats, each representing a different stage in my life according to their adoption dates. I connected these abstract pieces with charcoal drawings of each cat, uniting each stage with a common material.

artworks.title: Soft
artworks.medium: Yarn, fabric, thread, beads, fabric dye + paint, water-based resist, terracotta, nail polish
artworks.description: In this piece, I organized some of my previous work, hoping to explore how different aspects of my life conflict with each other in the form of a bed. I made this work to demonstrate the tenderness with which I now view these characteristics.

artworks.title: Shrouded by Waves
artworks.medium: BFK paper, gouache, colored pencil, linocut, water-based ink
artworks.description: In this piece, I rendered childhood pictures of myself, layering a linocut of waves as a reference to my old name. I made this piece to depict the rose-tinted glasses that time places over my childhood.

artworks.title: Comfort
artworks.medium: Yarn, fabric, thread, beads, fabric dye + paint, water-based resist, terracotta, nail polish, me
artworks.description: Expanding on previous ideas, I made this piece to incorporate myself within the composition and solidify the comfort I find within my identity.

artworks.title: Familial Still Life
artworks.medium: Graphite
artworks.description: This piece was made for my drawing class in school. I reimagined the exercise of still-life drawing by arranging objects representing family members into a triangular, path-like composition. Older generations anchor the bottom, while my sister and I are near the top, the product of those who came before us.

artworks.title: Salad Bowl of America
artworks.medium: Acrylic paint and collage
artworks.description: In this piece, I depict the hands of five of my friends, which stem from collages of artifacts from the Smithsonian that align with their respective cultures. I made this piece to convey that there is no fixed definition of what being American is.
artworks.alt: Painting titled Salad Bowl of America.

artworks.title: Home?
artworks.medium: Popsicle sticks, colored pencil, newsprint, wood glue, hot glue
artworks.description: In this piece, I drew memories from the past to represent how they become more conceptual with age. I made this piece to allude to how my current perception of my childhood is different from how it actually was.
artworks.alt: Mixed media sculpture titled Home? built with popsicle sticks, newsprint, and colored pencil.

artworks.title: From the Bush
artworks.medium: Wire mesh, Chinese rice paper, acrylic paint, watercolor, golden gel gloss
artworks.description: By manipulating wire mesh that is reminiscent of garden trellises and painting on the paper that I used to wrap this mesh, I created zucchini and its leaves as a reference to my family’s connection with gardening.

artworks.title: Peeking Through
artworks.medium: BFK paper, legion drawing paper, linocut, water-based ink, golden soft gel, yarn, screws
artworks.description: In this piece, I stitched colored pencil portraits of myself together to create a fabric that is my childhood. I layered linoprinted alyssums that represent who I am today. This composition suggests that my childhood self is not gone as I thought before but rather still influencing my current self.

artworks.title: Anxieties
artworks.medium: Metal rings, yarn, crochet, cyanotype
artworks.description: I made this piece to capture how ruminating thoughts can control me by using crochet, a hobby that I often engage in when stressed. The net constricts the shirt and makes it take another shape, similar to how anxiety changes who I am.

artworks.title: Caught
artworks.medium: Metal rings, yarn, crochet, cyanotype
artworks.description: I made this piece to encapsulate how it feels to be caught between the expectations of two different worlds. The crocheted nets symbolize the anxiety caused by societal expectations. The background of my mother's garden represents familial pressures, while my outfit alludes to expectations on how I should act to conform to American societal rules.

artworks.title: Dinnertime
artworks.medium: Oil paint, acrylic paint, canvas, perforated plastic non-slip mat painted with acrylics, needle and thread, yarn, metal mesh, wood panel, knitted garments, cyanotype prints, mirror
artworks.description: In this piece, I use my art as a backdrop for a dinner scene that features my parents. I made this piece to solidify my family’s influence on my art by including them as a part of my artwork.

artworks.title: Sketchbook Page
artworks.medium: Colored pencils
artworks.description: In my free time, I enjoy volunteering at the Harvard Natural History Museum. This is a spread from my sketchbook where I enjoyed rendering the shine of precious stones.
